key_insight: Each decode step's weight and KV sweep does restore its rows. A 1-bit-per-row coverage map lets the controller skip refresh for rows already read.
killer_doubt: Decode steps of ~20-50 ms straddle the 32 ms tREFW (16 ms hot), and idle KV stays unread. Refresh is only ~5-20% of bandwidth, and REF-borne TRR is lost.
decisive_experiment: Replay vLLM decode traces (dense 70B and MoE) through a Ramulator2 HBM3 model with a row-coverage bitmap. If >20% of rows miss a 32 ms window, stop. <$50k.
prior_art: Smart Refresh (Ghosh and Lee, MICRO 2007) skips refresh for recently accessed rows; RANA (ISCA 2018) for NN eDRAM; Phase B N-73, N-64.

key_insight: Analog accumulators on every 4-row group track all rows with no read-modify-write, so many-sided patterns cannot evade them and PRAC's tRC penalty goes away.
killer_doubt: A designed 64 ms leak on ~1 fF is ~8 fA and drifts ~100x over 25-95 C; packet mismatch ~10%. Workaround: no leak, reset on REF. Micron patents the core.
decisive_experiment: 28 nm MPW: 4,096 analog counters (coupling-cap pump, reset-on-REF, single-transistor trip). Measure trip-count spread, leakage tail and temperature drift at 25-110 C. ~$300k.
prior_art: Micron analog accumulator patents US 10,964,378, US 11,568,918 and US 10,943,636 (via search snippet); JEDEC DDR5 PRAC digital per-row counters.

key_insight: Precision becomes a fetch knob: bit-plane columns plus micro-row activation move only the planes a kernel needs. Useful for any-precision weights and KV top-k scoring.
killer_doubt: Weights already ship stored at FP8 or INT4. Keeping 16-bit planes so you can read 4 costs 4x capacity. Only multi-precision serving gains, likely ~1.5-3x.
decisive_experiment: GPU emulation of an Any-Precision-style bit-plane layout serving mixed 4/8/16-bit requests on a 70B model. Measure bytes moved and accuracy against separate quantized copies. <$50k.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (ICML 2024) bit-plane weights; FGDRAM and Half-DRAM fine-grained activation; SIMDRAM vertical layout; Phase B N-70.

key_insight: A nm-scale c-Si buried channel holds ~1e-7 bulk traps per stage and negligible dark charge. Regenerating each 64-stage loop relaxes the CTE need to ~0.9995.
killer_doubt: A 2-phase stage is at least 4F^2 per packet, so at CIS F=45 nm a bit takes ~10x DRAM's area. One amp per 64 bits is 16x DRAM's amp count.
decisive_experiment: 65 nm CIS MPW: 64-stage overlapping-gate buried-channel loop. Measure CTE from 10 MHz to 4 GHz, and 4-level packet error after 1e6 regenerated rotations. ~$250k.
prior_art: Intel 2416 and Fairchild CCD memories (1970s); imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024, 3D IMW 2026; logged in s2-innovation-R16).

key_insight: Small wells make dark charge minor: 1,600 nm2 at 1 nA/cm2 gives ~0.1 e/s. CID column reads move charge without destroying it.
killer_doubt: A 40x40 nm MOS well holds ~230 e: ~1 mV on a 35 fF column versus ~20 e read noise. 3 bits needs ~100x averaging; writing needs an injecting junction.
decisive_experiment: University-fab 32x32 CID array at 0.5-1 um with TCAD scaling. Measure electrical (non-optical) write selectivity, half-select disturb and correlated-double-sampled column SNR. ~$150k.
prior_art: GE charge-injection-device imagers (Michon and Burke, 1970s); 1970s planar MOS-capacitor DRAM cells; CCD memories.

key_insight: Skipping restore for data that is never re-read saves the bitline swing, CV^2/2: ~17 fJ per 35 fF pair, ~140 pJ per 1 KB row. tRAS halves for those rows.
killer_doubt: Consumption must cover a whole row (8 KB per rank). KV caches and weights are re-read every token, so read-once traffic is likely <5% of activations.
decisive_experiment: Trace study across LLM serving, networking and analytics: measure the fraction of activations whose entire row is dead after the read. If <10%, stop. ~$50k.
prior_art: IBM destructive-read eDRAM architecture proposals (~2000s, from memory); restore truncation (HPCA 2016); isolated offset-cancelling SAs; Phase B N-64.

key_insight: Retention-limited fails improve ~2x per 10 C. Dies that fail only above 75 C stay usable in cold-plate or immersion-cooled servers.
killer_doubt: Temperature grades and downgrade channels already exist. Hot-only margin fallout after repair is likely ~1-3%. HBM next to a GPU runs 85-95 C even when liquid-cooled.
decisive_experiment: With one vendor or OSAT, re-test 10k hot-test rejects at 60 C with 2x margin and a VRT soak. If <2% of output is recovered, stop. ~$150k.
prior_art: Commercial vs industrial temperature grades; Micron SpecTek downgraded components; DDR5 2x refresh above 85 C.

key_insight: Retired DDR4 is zero-capex supply during a ~4x price spike. The CXL card's controller absorbs aging through retention profiling, chipkill and row remap.
killer_doubt: Already deployed: Microsoft GreenSKU runs reused DDR4 behind CXL. The card and controller add ~$0.3-0.8/GB and 70-150 ns, so it suits cold-tier pages only.
decisive_experiment: Buy 500 retired RDIMMs. Profile retention and VRT on an FPGA CXL card for 30 days at 85 C, then compare landed $/GB with shipping Structera-class cards. ~$200k.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X DDR4 reuse; ITRenew decommissioned-hardware resale.

key_insight: The same reuse play as I-03344, through a custom buffer chip. The water argument holds: a reused GB avoids nearly all of its fab water.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-03344. A buffer chip cannot reach the DRAM's internal sense amps, so weak-column sensing reduces to timing-margin tests. An ASIC tapeout costs ~$10-30M.
decisive_experiment: Fold into I-03344. Run its FPGA profiling first, and tape out an ASIC only if profiling qualifies >90% of retired DIMMs at <$0.5/GB landed.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU; Marvell Structera X and Astera Leo CXL controllers; batch-mate I-03344.

key_insight: Slow SA resolution marks near-threshold bits as erasures. Known-location errors cost half the parity: 4 erasures per 512 bits need only a d=5 code (~20 bits, 3.9%).
killer_doubt: Fully leaked junction/GIDL tail cells read confidently wrong and unflagged. If >50% of errors at 2-4x tREFI are confident, gain falls to ~15% parity. Flag latch: ~3-7% die.
decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender on DDR4/DDR5: read each row at reduced and nominal tRCD and treat mismatches as erasure flags. Measure the flagged fraction of retention and low-margin errors at 2-8x tREFI. ~$80k.
prior_art: NAND soft-decision LDPC; Razor delayed-sample timing detection (MICRO 2003); XED on-die error flags (ISCA 2016); FLY-DRAM; Phase B N-62.

key_insight: Moving addressing out of the array into a relaxed-pitch emitter array would remove per-bit transistors, wordlines and EUV, if beams could write reliably.
killer_doubt: An 8x8 nm nitride spot holds ~1-6 trapped electrons (1e12-1e13 cm^-2). At ~1e15 e/cm2 per write, ~1 C/cm2 oxide damage arrives within ~1e3-1e4 cycles.
decisive_experiment: In a commercial SEM, write and read 8 nm charge spots on an ONO film. Cycle 1e6 times, and measure retention, read disturb and signal per spot. ~$100k.
prior_art: GE BEAMOS and Control Data EBAM (1970s); HP Atomic Resolution Storage, field emitters on phase-change media (~2000); IBM MEMS microcolumns.

key_insight: Avalanche gain makes ~100 stored electrons an almost certain trigger: at PDP 0.5, 1-0.5^100 is ~1. Sensing is not the limit.
killer_doubt: 100 e retained 64 ms needs leakage <=0.13 fA, ~100x below the 13 fA Si tail. Low-DCR SPADs need ~10+ V and um guard rings, not 30-40 nm pitch.
decisive_experiment: 40 nm CMOS test chip: transfer 100-500 e packets into gated SPADs at 1 um pitch. Measure trigger and false-trigger rates and the junction-leakage tail at 85 C. ~$300k.
prior_art: Z-RAM impact-ionisation floating body (Innovative Silicon); EMCCD gain registers; Fossum quanta-image-sensor jots read single electrons without avalanche.
